// The prompt for finding how a project is built, run, and tested, so each
// way becomes a button. <projectDir> is filled in with the project's folder.

export anchor RunTargets:
    intro:
        We want to be able to run the project in <projectDir> with a button,
        whatever kind of project it is. Only read files, and don't change
        anything, and don't run anything.

    task:
        Look through the project to find how it is built, run, and tested:
        its build files and manifests, such as Cargo.toml, package.json,
        CMakeLists.txt, Makefile, pyproject.toml, go.mod, or build.gradle, its
        scripts, and its readme. Work out a shell command for each way worth a
        button, run from the project's folder. The first is the way to run
        the project itself, from scratch: on a fresh clone it has to work, so
        it builds first when the project must be built, as with cmake
        configuring and building, then running the binary it built. Then add
        building on its own, and running the tests, when the project has them,
        and anything else a developer here would run often, such as a dev
        server, a linter, or formatting. Give each a short name, such as Run,
        Build, or Test, and its kind: run, build, test, or other. Prefer the
        project's own scripts and tools to invented ones, and keep to at most
        eight.

    replyFormat:
        Reply with nothing but JSON, in this form:
        \ {"targets": [{"name": "Run", "command": "cargo run", "kind": "run"}]} \

- [Ctrl+Shift+F5 (Cmd+Shift+F5 on macOS) runs the project's release run target, as pressing its button does](spec/scope/run-targets/index.pi)

- [The harness adds a release run target where the project has a release build](spec/scope/run-targets/index.pi)
- [Without a release target the shortcut does nothing](spec/scope/run-targets/index.pi)
- [Ctrl+F5 runs the primary target, or finds how to run the project](spec/scope/run-targets/index.pi)
- [run.json is kept with the project and can be edited by hand](spec/scope/run-targets/index.pi)
EOF

def edit(p,pairs):
    s=open(p).read()

        assert s.count(o)==1,(p,o[:50]); s=s.replace(o,n)
    open(p,'w').write(s)
edit('spec/scope/run-targets/index.pi',[
('''        - other, anything else, with a terminal icon
''','''        - other, anything else, with a terminal icon

        A run target can also be marked release: it runs the project from an
        optimized release build, such as `cargo run --release`, rather than
        the build it is developed with. At most one target is marked release.
'''),
('''            The harness replies with JSON listing each target's name, command,
            and kind. A target with no name or no command is left out, as is a
            kind that isn't one of the four, which counts as other. A reply
            with no targets at all fails, saving nothing.''','''            The harness replies with JSON listing each target's name, command,
            and kind, and whether it is the release run. Where the project has
            a release build, it adds a release run target, named "Run Release"

            command is left out, as is a kind that isn't one of the four, which
            counts as other. Past the first target marked release, none is. A
            reply with no targets at all fails, saving nothing.'''),
('''        The tooltip of whichever of the two buttons it presses gives it. It
        does nothing without a project, or while an inset panel other than the
        Run panel is open.''','''        The tooltip of whichever of the two buttons it presses gives it. It
        does nothing without a project, or while an inset panel other than the
        Run panel is open.

        <Ctrl+Shift+F5> (<Cmd+Shift+F5> on macOS) runs the target marked
        release in the same way, and its button's tooltip gives it. Where the
        project has no release target, such as when it has no release build,
        or its targets were found before release ones were, it does nothing.
        It is otherwise as <Ctrl+F5>.'''),
])
edit('system-prompts/run-targets.pi',[
('''        Build, or Test, and its kind: run, build, test, or other. Prefer the''','''        Build, or Test, and its kind: run, build, test, or other. Where the
        project has a release build, as a Rust project's cargo run --release
        or a CMake project configured for Release, add one more run target,
        right after the way to run the project, that runs it from a release
        build, named Run Release, and mark it as the release. Prefer the'''),
('''        \\ {"targets": [{"name": "Run", "command": "cargo run", "kind": "run"}]} \\''','''        \\ {"targets": [{"name": "Run", "command": "cargo run", "kind": "run"}, {"name": "Run Release", "command": "cargo run --release", "kind": "run", "release": true}]} \\'''),
])
EOF

content.text:
Ctrl+Shift+F5 (Cmd+Shift+F5 on macOS) now runs the project's release run target, just like pressing its button. If the project has no release target it does nothing. The spec builds, and the run test now checks both cases; 274 of 275 tests pass, the one failure being the same `...`/`…` default-prompt test as before. I haven't tried it in the running app.

**Existing projects won't have a release target yet.** Their saved run targets were found before this change, so press **Find Again** once, or add `"release": true` to a target in `.suspense/run.json` by hand.

**How a release target is marked:** a run target can now carry `"release": true`, meaning it runs the project from an optimized release build.
- When finding targets, the harness is asked to add a "Run Release" button right after "Run" wherever the project has a release build, for example `cargo run --release` or a CMake Release configuration. This change to the built-in prompt hasn't been tried against a real harness run.
- Only one target can be the release one; if the harness marks several, only the first counts.

**Behaviour:** otherwise the same as Ctrl+F5:
- Pressing it again while the release target runs brings its panel back.
- It does nothing while any other inset panel is open.
- The release button's tooltip shows the shortcut.

**Changes:**
- **Spec (`spec/scope/run-targets/index.pi`):** the release marking, the harness reply, and the new shortcut.
- **Built-in prompt (`system-prompts/run-targets.pi`):** asks for the release target.
- **Code:**
  - `src/run_targets.rs`: the release marking.
  - `src/ribbon/mod.rs`: the new shortcut.
  - `src/main_window.rs`: running the release target when it's pressed.
  - `src/ribbon/code_tab.rs`: the tooltip.
- **Tests:** checks that only the first release target counts. The run test also presses Ctrl+Shift+F5 twice: with no release target nothing runs, and with one saved, it runs.

**Existing projects won't have a release target yet.** Their saved run targets were found before this change, so press **Find Again** once, or add `"release": true` to a target in `.suspense/run.json` by hand.

**How a release target is marked:** a run target can now carry `"release": true`, meaning it runs the project from an optimized release build.
- When finding targets, the harness is asked to add a "Run Release" button right after "Run" wherever the project has a release build, for example `cargo run --release` or a CMake Release configuration. This change to the built-in prompt hasn't been tried against a real harness run.
- Only one target can be the release one; if the harness marks several, only the first counts.

**Behaviour:** otherwise the same as Ctrl+F5:
- Pressing it again while the release target runs brings its panel back.
- It does nothing while any other inset panel is open.
- The release button's tooltip shows the shortcut.

**Changes:**
- **Spec (`spec/scope/run-targets/index.pi`):** the release marking, the harness reply, and the new shortcut.
- **Built-in prompt (`system-prompts/run-targets.pi`):** asks for the release target.
- **Code:**
  - `src/run_targets.rs`: the release marking.
  - `src/ribbon/mod.rs`: the new shortcut.
  - `src/main_window.rs`: running the release target when it's pressed.
  - `src/ribbon/code_tab.rs`: the tooltip.
- **Tests:** checks that only the first release target counts. The run test also presses Ctrl+Shift+F5 twice: with no release target nothing runs, and with one saved, it runs.
